items.text: Mohammad Reza Bahonar stated that the enemy's goal in the imposed war was to tire the nation and create a gap between the people and the Imam. He added that the enemy uses the tactic of creating a "war and no war" dichotomy among the people. Bahonar also emphasized that negotiation is a continuation of the Sacred Defense.

Chris Wright, the US Energy Secretary, stated that the average oil flow from the Strait of Hormuz has reached about 13 million barrels per day. On one day last week, more than 20 million barrels of oil passed through the strait, exceeding pre-conflict levels. He also mentioned that current pressure on energy prices is mainly due to refining capacity limits.

A group of Iranians residing in Sweden marched against the Islamic Republic on Saturday, October 4, in the streets of Gothenburg. This video was released by Iran International. The march was held in protest against the Islamic Republic.

Hamid Bord, CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company, stated that the enemy has planned to attack oil facilities. He urged people to save 10 to 15 percent of energy consumption to ensure continuous energy supply. Additionally, records for oil and gas production in Iran have been broken.

Mousa Al-Reza Badagh Abadi, detained during the December 2025 protests, was sentenced to one year in prison by the Appeals Court of North Khorasan Province. The sentence was issued on charges of "propaganda against the regime." The same sentence had previously been issued in the primary court.

Donald Trump rejected the proposal to return to the Islamabad agreement. Ali Shirazi, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said that the Strait of Hormuz has turned against the Islamic Republic and the pressure from its insecurity now affects the Islamic Republic itself. He added that the US economic pressure policy has put pressure on the Islamic Republic's economy, as the Treasury Secretary stated.

A group of Iranians living in the US held a car caravan on Saturday, October 4, in San Jose, California. They carried the Lion and Sun flags. This event was reported based on videos received by Iran International.

The Israeli army announced that Saher Nidal Lotfi Saqr was killed on Saturday in an attack on the Nasirat area of Gaza. He was a member of a terrorist group affiliated with global jihadist organizations. Saqr supplied weapons for Hamas during the war.

Individuals involved in organizing the 10-kilometer Tehran marathon, including the head of Tehran athletics and provincial sports officials, have been summoned to the prosecutor's office. So far, one person has been charged and released on bail. Tehran's prosecutor has filed charges against the organizers for violating legal and religious regulations.

Reuters reported that security measures have been tightened at the Royal Air Force base in Fairford, UK, used for operations against Iran. Roadblocks and armed police have restricted access to the base. The US Air Force stated that its forces in the UK remain alert and are taking protective measures.

The Israeli army announced that in response to the launch of an explosive drone by Hezbollah towards its forces in southern Lebanon, it targeted the group's positions. The launch sites of drones and anti-tank missiles were targeted in the attacks. The Israeli army warned that any use of force from Lebanese territory will be met with a decisive response.

The Ministry of Health has halved the medical entrance exam capacity this year. In regions like Baluchistan and Lenjan, power outages continue, causing difficulties for people. Additionally, the cost of stationery has risen sharply.

Ali Mehri, a 16-year-old teenager, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Zarrinshahr, Isfahan, due to a war bullet hitting his neck. Videos show his family's distress during his birthday ceremony at his grave.

Amir Hatami, the commander of the army, said the war is not over and the victory must be maintained. He emphasized that the enemy has suffered heavy blows and its credibility is collapsing. He also mentioned that the enemy does not know how to deal with the 90 million people of Iran.

Matlab Ahmadian, a political prisoner in Evin prison, is serving his sixteenth year of imprisonment and suffers from multiple illnesses. Forensic medicine has confirmed his inability to endure imprisonment, but the Tehran prosecutor has opposed stopping the sentence or granting medical leave. Delays in transferring him to medical centers have worsened his health conditions.

Iran International is launching the Farahnaz Espad scholarship in memory of one of its first presenters. This scholarship is awarded annually to Iranian students for master's studies abroad, focusing on human rights with an emphasis on women's rights. The scholarship amount is 40,000 pounds, and applications open every year on March 10.

A Hamas member who obtained asylum and citizenship in the UK is accused of planning attacks against Jewish and Israeli targets in Europe. This individual is the son of a senior Hamas official and previously worked in Ismail Haniyeh's security team. He applied for asylum in 2015 and later received UK citizenship.

The prison sentence and media activity ban for Sadegh Zibakalam were confirmed by the judicial authority. He was sentenced to one year in prison and a two-year media activity ban in the primary court. The prison sentence has also been suspended for three years.

Yesterday, rental drivers working in the transportation unit of Tabriz Municipality protested against poor job conditions and low wages and benefits in front of the City Council building. The protest was held to express their job dissatisfaction. The drivers demand better working conditions.

A video shows Meysam Hazini's daughter expressing her longing for her father on her first day of school. Meysam Hazini, 37 years old, was killed on January 9, 2026, in Gorgan. The video captures the daughter's emotions in her father's absence.

Reyhaneh Karimi won the bronze medal in the 77 kg category at the Nagoya Asian Games with a total of 243 kg. She became the first female weightlifter from Iran to win a medal in these games. The representative from China won gold and the representative from Kazakhstan won silver.

Mohammad Seraj, a member of the Social Commission of the Parliament, said that Americans know the president and foreign minister of Iran are not decision-makers, which is why Trump did not accept the Islamic Republic's conditions. He emphasized that Iran's major foreign policies are determined by the leadership. Seraj also linked the official government positions to statements by Mohsen Rezaei.

Loghman Sharifi from the Supreme Council of the Nursing Organization stated that nurses' monthly income does not even cover the expenses of the first 10 days of the month. He added that the salary increase for nurses does not match the inflation rate, worsening their livelihood problems. He also demanded the implementation of governance job benefits and salary increases in line with inflation.

The Iran Trade Development Organization announced that the import of South Korean home appliances is only allowed in a limited manner through porters, sailors, and border cooperatives. Official import of large home appliances remains prohibited. This decision follows a 2021 order by Ali Khamenei banning the import of these goods.

In Mehr 1402, students faced financial difficulties in purchasing books and stationery. Some students were barred from classes due to unpaid tuition. Additionally, discussions about hijab and jihad tabeen took place in some schools.

Fars News Agency, citing a source close to Iran's negotiation team, reported that Tehran is determined not to yield its rights and interests under pressure from the US and Israel. The source mentioned internal challenges in the US and dissatisfaction with the consequences of war. Iran's recent proposal includes phased and reciprocal measures.

Mohammad Akraminia, the army spokesperson, said that the US is not in a good position in the region and might launch an attack. He added that Iran is better prepared than before and has optimized its equipment. He also warned that if the enemy attacks, the region will face more conflict and unrest.

Abbas Abdi was sentenced to one year of imprisonment by the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province. The Etemad newspaper was also sentenced to a two-month suspension of activity. This ruling is related to a specific case.

The video shows Bahram Yousefi's son going to school on his first day without his father. Bahram Yousefi, 29 years old, was killed on January 8, 2026, in Naziabad, Tehran. This incident has drawn attention.

With the start of the new school year, citizens have protested the sharp increase in stationery prices and school expenses. In Shiraz and Isfahan, students have been banned from entering schools due to unpaid tuition. This issue has put heavy pressure on families.

The Italian Senate passed a new sustainable nuclear energy law. According to this law, the government has the authority to regulate the construction and operation of nuclear power plants and manage spent fuel and nuclear waste. This report was provided by Sadaf Baghbani from Iran International.

Ali Alirezaei, a student at Sharif University of Technology, was sentenced to four years in prison. He had previously been expelled and banned from studying by the university's disciplinary committee. This sentence was issued by the judicial authority.

Han Zheng, Vice President of China, emphasized the special responsibilities of major powers in maintaining international peace and security. He called for respect for the sovereignty and security of Middle Eastern countries and the stability of global trade. He also stressed adherence to international laws and the rule of law.

The prosecutor of Yazd announced that alcoholic beverages were discovered and confiscated during an inspection of a cafe. Alcohol tests were conducted on 100 people present, with 21 testing positive. The cafe was sealed by judicial order and a case was filed for legal proceedings.

The appellate court confirmed the conviction of Ali Younesi, a political prisoner. He was sentenced to five years in prison for supporting the Zionist regime and 15 months for propaganda against the regime. This sentence was issued in a case opened against him during his imprisonment.

Sergey Lavrov, Russia's foreign minister, called the use of force to kill Ali Khamenei and his family unacceptable. He also accused the US and Israel of targeting Iran's civilian infrastructure and nuclear facilities. These remarks were made at the UN General Assembly.

The government has announced difficulties in supplying textbooks, and delivery may take up to two months. Schools in District 8 of Tehran have a security atmosphere with surveillance cameras installed in classrooms. Azad University of Kordkuy is also facing issues with reopening classes and student entry control.

The Central Bank of Iran's report shows the annual inflation rate in September exceeded 68 percent. This is the highest inflation rate since 1943. The point-to-point inflation rate in September was about 84 percent, and the point-to-point inflation for goods was over 118 percent.

Poria Bagheri's father responded to Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks about foreign involvement in the December 2025 killings, questioning why the internet was cut and cameras removed if the perpetrators were foreign. He also asked how government rallies were held safely. Poria Bagheri, 22, was killed on the evening of December 8, 2025, in Shahriar.
Amirhossein Mohseni Pour and Milad Kariminasab, political prisoners in Dehdasht prison, were granted leave. This leave was granted on Thursday, 2 Mehr. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Heshmatollah Falahatpisheh was sentenced to one year in prison by the appeals court for publishing content on social media. The execution of the sentence has been suspended for five years. The sentence was issued by the appeals court.
A video has been released showing a parade of Basij and IRGC forces in Dezful. The parade took place on Thursday, the 24th of September. The video shows military equipment and a Dushka.

Moshkat-ol-Zahra Safi and Mandegar Farzami won their first-round singles matches at the 2026 Nagoya Asian Games. These two players recorded the first singles wins in the history of Iranian women's tennis at these games. Both Farzami and Safi defeated their opponents in straight sets.

Internet in many cities of Iran, including Bushehr, Iranshahr, Birjand, and Fardis, has experienced disruptions and outages. The infrastructure company denies that these outages are due to updates and states that the Supreme National Security Council made the decision. Users have reported low speeds, high costs, and difficulties accessing systems and websites.

The mothers of Iliya Valipour and Armin Timoori-rad met at Iliya Valipour's grave. Iliya Valipour, 18 years old, was killed on January 8, 2026, in Karaj. Armin Timoori-rad, 19 years old, was killed on January 9 in Fardis.

Belgian security authorities stated that the perpetrators of two terrorist attacks in Liège and Antwerp followed the Islamic Republic's call to target Jewish and Israeli interests. Last March, a bomb exploded in front of a synagogue in Liège and a car was set on fire in the Jewish neighborhood of Antwerp. The coordinator of these attacks was arrested in Turkey.

The Ministry of Science has issued the 'Guidelines for Decorum, Ethics, and University Conduct' to universities. According to this directive, wearing attire compatible with Iranian-Islamic culture is mandatory for entering university premises. Universities are required to inform students about this guideline.

Shahram Kholdi said China does not want to accept the Islamic Republic as a cost in its competition with the US. Beijing tries to maintain a safe distance from the Islamic Republic due to its extensive economic relations with Arab countries. He warned that the Islamic Republic may become a burnt pawn that even China will eventually distance itself from.

A chip factory in Abik, Tehran province, is not unloading about 200 truckloads of potatoes due to a sharp decline in sales. Drivers have been waiting in the factory area for about two days. This issue was reported to Iran International by a citizen.

Donald Trump stated that oil prices will sharply drop once Iran surrenders and the war ends. He mentioned that food prices and almost all prices have decreased. Trump also announced a record amount of oil transferred through the Strait of Hormuz.
On Saturday, 4th of Mehr, in the Sungun copper mine in Varzeqan, an 18-year-old worker died due to a soil collapse and another worker was injured.

British police arrested five men after reports of three suspicious vehicles moving towards the Royal Air Force base at Fairford. The men were detained on suspicion of offenses under the Explosives Act and remain in custody. Police evacuated 85 households and established a 400-meter radius perimeter for the army's bomb disposal unit to investigate.

Mothers seeking justice for the deceased Parisa Amini, Armin Teimoorzadeh, Ilya Valipour, Tanya Abbasi, and Pouria Bagheri lit candles together. They joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." The video has been released.

Ashkan Madani was arrested on September 15 to serve his prison sentence and transferred to Evin Prison. He had previously been sentenced to four years and seven months in prison. Since his arrest, he has had only one phone call with his family.

The spokesperson for the Houthi armed forces in Yemen stated that Saudi F-15 fighter jets launched attacks from Khamis Mushait base on the Taiz market and the Khab and Al-Shaaf areas in Al-Jawf province. The attacks targeted the Taiz market in Ma'awiyah twice and Khab and Al-Shaaf four times. He warned that the bloodshed in the Ma'awiyah market will have severe consequences for Saudi Arabia.

Pressure on the families of those killed in the December protests continues. The family of Ahmad Ghasempour Pilehroodi has faced increased pressure after opposing his registration as a martyr and Basiji. More details were provided by Farnoush Faraji from Iran International.

Reyhaneh Karimi won the first medal in the history of Iranian women's weightlifting at the Asian Games. This event marks a historic achievement for Iranian women's sports. The report was prepared by Alireza Modiri.

Abdolmahdi Asadi stated that with the suspension of Oman flights, mobile phone imports to Iran have stopped. Over 90% of the country's mobile phones are imported by air. This flight suspension has caused problems in goods imports.

A judicial case has been filed against Shahram Azmoudeh, a retired teacher and editor of Talash monthly. He is accused of propaganda against the regime and has been summoned to the first investigative branch of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office in Talesh. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

At the end of the eighth day of the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Iran dropped one place to eighth in the medal table. Reyhaneh Karimi won a bronze medal in the 77 kg weightlifting category. Iran's team currently has 7 gold, 14 silver, and 8 bronze medals.

Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran is fully prepared to resume war with the United States and will stand firm against any attack. He also said Tehran is ready for diplomacy and has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran demands the release of blocked assets and the ability to sell oil in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

Sarina Naqsh was eliminated in the women's boxing quarterfinals after losing to a North Korean opponent. Amir Esmaeili advanced to the semifinals by defeating a Chinese opponent and secured a bronze medal. Interviews were conducted with former and current Iranian boxing athletes.
Babak Roshanzamir from Likak was arrested by security forces on September 17. He was transferred to Dehdasht prison after about a week. This news was reported by Harana news agency.

The appeals court confirmed an additional five-year prison sentence for Ali Younesi, a computer engineering student. This sentence was previously issued by Branch 29 of the Revolutionary Court. Ali Younesi and Amirhossein Moradi remain in prison and are barred from continuing their education.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that China has significantly reduced its assistance to Iran and denied reports of increased military and intelligence aid. He added that only about 15 million barrels of Iranian oil remain at sea, and likely the final shipments to China will be delivered in the next two weeks, after which Tehran will have nothing to trade and, due to this pressure, seeks a deal. Bessent also said the US does not allow Iran's oil to exit, and Iran's share of oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz is zero.

Hamid Rasaei was sentenced to 10 months imprisonment and to publish a retraction. The court stated that the crime occurred before his parliamentary term and he is not immune from prosecution. He will present himself to serve the sentence.

Donald Trump announced that an unprecedented amount of oil was transferred through the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday night. He said this amount was higher than the oil transferred before the war began. Trump also emphasized that oil prices will sharply decrease once Iran surrenders and the war ends.

The municipality of the city of Vaughan north of Toronto is installing a plaque and bench in memory of the immortal figures of the Lion and Sun Revolution in a cultural center. This plan was approved a few months ago by the Vaughan city council. The unveiling ceremony will be held with the presence of Iranians.

Three men accused of kidnapping and assaulting two sisters in Tehran were sentenced to death, flogging, and imprisonment. Two other defendants in the case were also sentenced to flogging and imprisonment. The verdict was issued by the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province.
A citizen sent a video showing that syrups prepared for their child are expired. The expiration dates have been erased and fake labels attached. This issue was reported by Iran International.

Iran International is awarding a scholarship named after Farahnaz Espad on the 40th day after her passing. This scholarship will cover the tuition costs for at least one Iranian student pursuing a master's degree abroad. The initiative honors the dedicated and patriotic presenter of Iran International.

Five years after the ban on importing Korean home appliances, a limited import license for these goods has been issued. Ahmad Alavi stated that this decision is neither beneficial for border residents nor the national economy and called it a rent-seeking decision to circumvent US sanctions.

Kazem Gharibabadi responded to Scott Bassett's remarks about instructing countries on economic relations with Iran. He stated that independent governments determine their relations based on their own interests. He also emphasized that the era of imposing will through threats and sanctions is coming to an end.

The deputy of elementary education in Qazvin province announced the identification of 309 children out of school in the province. He claimed that all these children have been integrated into the education system.

British police arrested several people near RAF Fairford airbase on suspicion of explosive-related crimes. Bomb disposal forces were deployed and several houses were evacuated. Police described the incident as a "major event."

British counter-terrorism police are investigating a possible link between the Islamic Republic and a bomb plot at RAF Fairford. The origin of the foiled operation is still unknown. The UK Defense Secretary announced close cooperation with the US on this matter.

Amirsam Didar, a resident of Dehdasht, is currently serving his sentence in Dehdasht prison. He has been sentenced to a total of 8 years in prison and a fine of 10 million tomans. He was arrested about 10 days ago to serve his sentence and transferred to prison.

Poland and Lithuania are reviewing civilian evacuation plans and exit routes in the Suwałki Gap area due to the possibility of a Russian attack. Warsaw has also strengthened its air defenses in border areas. These measures are in response to regional security threats.

Hassan Pajani, a member of Iran's electronic football team, won the gold medal at the Nagoya Asian Games. He stated that training with good internet abroad was one reason for his success. Pajani has been living and training in Indonesia for the past year and a half.

John Kennedy, Republican senator from Louisiana, said Trump's administration rejected the Islamic Republic's proposal. He emphasized that sanctions and blockade should continue. He also mentioned the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and its impact on oil prices.

Hossein Ali Shahriari stated that the out-of-pocket payment share for patients has increased to between 55% and 75% this year, with some drug prices rising 400 to 500 percent. Payments to public hospitals are delayed by 10 to 12 months, forcing patients to procure some hospitalization supplies externally. Additionally, the health insurance organization's budget covered only half of the forecasted needs.

Tahereh Azarpayvand and Pardis Eidivandi, Iran's representatives in the women's under 57 kg kurash at the Nagoya Asian Games, were eliminated from the competition. Azarpayvand lost 5-0 in the quarterfinals. Eidivandi was also eliminated after a 5-0 defeat against a Filipino opponent following a bye in the first round.
Donald Trump did not rule out the possibility of another attack on Iran. He expects negotiations with Tehran to continue this week. These statements were made in an interview with Axios.

A 9-year-old child was injured in the head during a military shooting in the Jihadabad area of Saravan county on Thursday. The child died on Sunday, October 5, due to the severity of the injuries in the hospital. The child's father was also injured during the shooting.

A video shows a protester in Shiraz writing a slogan against the leader of the Islamic Republic on a wall. The slogan reads "Death to Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Zahhak." This video was released by Iran International.

The Iranian Parliament's Research Center estimated the electricity consumption of crypto miners in Iran at around 930 to 1200 megawatts, equivalent to about 6 percent of the country's total electricity shortfall during the four hot months of the year. The report also estimated the annual fuel cost for crypto mining at approximately 1.5 billion dollars, assuming the use of imported diesel.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said that including Iran's nuclear program in the negotiations and China's more active role have increased the likelihood of an agreement between Tehran and Washington. He added that military and economic pressures have strengthened the US position. The durability of any agreement depends on consensus within the Islamic Republic's power structure and the implementation of commitments.

Fatemeh Tousali and Yalda Hassan-Shokati competed in the women's trampoline preliminary round. Tousali advanced to the final by placing sixth, while Hassan-Shokati did not reach the final. The male representatives also failed to win a medal.

The spokesperson of Yemen's armed forces announced that four Iranian experts were killed in an operation against Houthi positions in Taiz province. In the past 72 hours, 752 targeted operations against the Houthis have been carried out. These operations resulted in the destruction of Houthi military equipment.
Hamid Ebrahimi's brother climbed Mount Sabalan on October 24 in memory of him. Hamid Ebrahimi was killed on January 8, 2026, in Gohardasht, Karaj. A video of this climb has been released.

The executive secretary of the Workers' House in Hamedan reported on the livelihood and medical problems of workers. Many workers cannot afford the heavy medical costs, and there is a shortage of specialist doctors in social security centers. High dental and joint disease treatment costs are also among the issues.

Mohammad Mahdi Shahriari said that Iran's exit from the NPT would mean building nuclear weapons, which Tehran does not intend to do. He added that such an exit would increase costs and tensions, and he doubts the exit proposal will pass in parliament. Shahriari also called for action against organized messaging encouraging representatives to vote for this proposal.
Trump announced that negotiations with Iran will resume this week. This news was shared in the audio version of Titrawol with Niousha Saremi. No further details were provided in the text.

The Netherlands national football team defeated Serbia 2-1 in their second UEFA Nations League match. Meerdink, who played his first match for the Netherlands just three days earlier, scored two goals after starting in the lineup. Additionally, Denmark defeated Wales 2-0.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said in the program "Cheshmandaz" that the Islamic Republic fears an explosion of public anger and possible overthrow more than war or famine. He described recent government actions as a sign of a large state of alert for possible suppression and killing. He also stated that the government has lost its trust in society.

Contract workers of Malard Municipality have complained about their unpaid wages. Employees at the Tehran office of Ghadir Petrochemical are concerned about job uncertainty. These issues have been reported in two different work units.
The Central Bank released a new report on the consumer price index in urban areas. The report shows that despite a decrease in the monthly growth rate of prices, inflation remains high.

The mother of Amirhossein Khodadadi responded to Masoud Pezeshkian's statements at the United Nations, demanding proof that her son was carrying a weapon. Amirhossein Khodadadi, 22 years old, was killed on the evening of January 8, 2026, in Najafabad.

Mohammad Reza Zenouzi said that there are many trophies on Monirieh Street and Esteghlal can even get a trophy at his expense. He criticized the new trend in Iranian football. This is while Ali Tajernia had claimed that the football federation promised to give the championship trophy of last season to Esteghlal.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, stated that France has deployed military equipment since the start of the war in Iran to protect its allies in the region. These deployments are entirely defensive, and France has not been targeted. The deployment of forces and equipment to Saudi Arabia will also be defensive and depend on Saudi requests and circumstances.

Cristiano Ronaldo was benched for Portugal after about four years. The Portuguese coach did not include him in the starting lineup against Norway and chose Gonçalo Ramos instead. Jorge Jesus explained the decision as managing Ronaldo's playtime in consecutive matches.

The New York Times and The Atlantic reported that the UAE and Egypt warned the Israeli Prime Minister before the October 7 attacks. Netanyahu did not take these warnings seriously and did not share them with security and military officials. This was discussed in an interview with Meir Javdanfar.

Basij forces are being urgently equipped with military and urban warfare equipment. This was discussed in the program Cheshmandaz with Mehdi Mahdavi Azad. The full version of the program is available on Iran International's YouTube channel.

The number of detained teacher union activists in Mamasani has reached six. These individuals were transferred to Noorabad Mamasani prison after interrogation. The arrests took place on Friday, September 24.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said the Islamic Republic needs economic openings more than before to buy time. He emphasized that merely selling oil is not enough for Tehran and access to oil revenues is crucial.

A source close to the Islamic Republic delegation in New York stated that there is no plan for a new round of negotiations with the US. Tehran's positions were conveyed to the American side through a Qatari mediator. Abbas Araghchi will return from New York on Tuesday after completing scheduled programs.

Fars News Agency reported that a sea cruise missile was fired at a violating ship in an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz. This news was based on local sources. Additionally, Iran International received a message from a local resident about a missile being fired from the shore towards the sea.

The mother of Farzin Poost-Ashkan Dorki went to the place where her son was killed after Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks at the United Nations. She expressed grief over her son's death and said he is being labeled a terrorist. This reaction was in response to Pezeshkian's statements.

The Fars Teachers' Trade Association reported the arrest of six union activists while visiting a sick colleague in Mamasani. These individuals were arrested without a warrant and transferred to Noorabad prison after interrogation. The charges against the detainees have not been disclosed.

The German national football team lost 1-0 to Greece in the second week of the UEFA Nations League. The match was held in Augsburg, and the only goal was scored by Korbelis in the 74th minute. Germany previously drew 1-1 against the Netherlands.

Leila Morvati said the parliament's plan on Strait of Hormuz security could lead to ship seizures and increased tensions with Washington. She added the law might complicate negotiations. Also, leaving the NPT and restrictions in the Strait could raise tensions.

Portugal's football team defeated Norway 2-1 in the second week of the UEFA Nations League. Coach Jorge Jesus kept Cristiano Ronaldo on the bench during the match. The goals for Portugal were scored by Felix and Ramos.

Bloomberg reported that two oil tankers linked to the Islamic Republic, seized during the 40-day war, are likely to reach the US in a few weeks. These tankers carry millions of dollars worth of Iranian crude oil that will be confiscated. The US Department of Justice has initiated legal proceedings to seize these tankers.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, stated on X that the US claims Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz, but the oil market has priced a significant premium. He attributed this contradiction either to the market or to the US narrative. Ghalibaf also mentioned that there is free dollar liquidity in the Strait of Hormuz available for anyone to take.

Donald Trump posted an image of the Strait of Hormuz map labeled as "Trump Strait" on his account. This occurred amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the US over this waterway. Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran has not yet received an official response from the US regarding its proposal.

Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi on Sunday, October 5, and met with Mohammed bin Zayed. This meeting took place amid closer ties between Israel and the UAE during the war with the Islamic Republic. Israel has also provided a temporary Iron Dome system to the UAE.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said that the Islamic Republic's pleas for a quick agreement with the US and willingness for direct negotiations indicate that the US blockade has been effective. He also pointed to Iran's concessions regarding the nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz.

Amir Giti stated that despite contradictory positions on war and negotiation, the Islamic Republic seeks to continue talks with the United States. It tries to convey its messages to Washington through intermediaries such as Qatar, Pakistan, and Turkey. The main issue is that the final decision-makers in cases like the Strait of Hormuz are not involved, leading to doubts about the Iranian delegation's ability to implement any agreement.

Maryam Dehkordi stated that the new directive from the Ministry of Intelligence continues the suppression of the student movement and pressures students to accept mandatory dress codes. Since the 1401 uprising, university environments have become more securitized, with students facing disciplinary actions and case filings. The confirmation of some students' sentences and recent arrests sends a threatening message from the judiciary to the student body.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the position of the Islamic Republic has become weaker and more fragile compared to the past. He added that it is still difficult for the Islamic Republic to accept people's demands or surrender to the US.

Mohammad Reza Aref stated that 250 million cubic meters of gas have been lost from the network due to damage in two recent wars. The government is trying to restore 100 million cubic meters of gas to the network before the cold season and may implement some blackouts to supply energy to industries. Additionally, energy for high-consumption households will be billed at full cost.

Ramin Kashif Azar, CEO of Imam Khomeini Airport, stated that flights from this airport continue to more than 30 international destinations, with over 60 flights operated today. He said the airport is fully operational and urged passengers to check official sources for schedule changes. These remarks come as some Iranian flights have been limited due to new US sanctions.

The Iranian national football team will play a friendly match against Russia in the second FIFA international window. Russian teams have been banned from official competitions following the Ukraine war. This match is held under special circumstances.

The CENTCOM spokesperson denied the IRGC's claim of seizing a US unmanned underwater vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The US stated it maintains control over all its vessels and drones. Previously, the IRGC claimed to have seized the vessel and declared the Strait of Hormuz closed.

Mark Kelly, a Democratic senator, criticized Donald Trump's handling of the war with Iran, calling it a 'disaster' and a 'mistake'. He said Trump entered the war without a strategic goal, plan, timeline, or exit strategy and is trapped.

Morgan Ortagus, former US envoy for Middle East affairs, said in an interview with Fox News that Iran's government is 'hanging by a thread' and the US blockade has isolated Tehran. She said Iran is not putting even a drop of oil on the free market, and nothing is being traded. Ortagus added that messages from Islamic Republic officials were incoherent last week, with leaders trying to meet with US and European officials on the sidelines while IRGC commanders were scolding them.

The one-day conference "Iran Alternative" was held on October 4 in Cologne, initiated by the Women, Life, Freedom network. The goal was to form a coordination and leadership council and explore ways to organize forces opposing the Islamic Republic. The meeting emphasized women's rights equality, ending discrimination, and minority rights.

Haaretz wrote in an analysis that both Iran and the US see the passage of time as beneficial to themselves, which could prolong the deadlock. Washington hopes economic pressure will force Iran to make concessions, while Iran sees limited US tolerance for ongoing costs. The expectation of mutual withdrawal may lead to escalation.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that Trump should not be appeased but controlled by raising the cost of war and missile pressure. Kayhan considers maintaining leverage over the Strait of Hormuz and energy routes as the only logical approach. The newspaper also criticized Iran's diplomatic stance in New York and the display of eagerness for negotiation.

Salar Velayatmadar stated that if the US attacks Iranian territory, the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab will be closed.
